scene: Static: 6-inch corner reflector at 3.251 m on shelving, cardboard box at 2.083 m, operator out of room.
method: LDC1 WRITE one register, read back, capture ~28 frames tagged with the new register generation, compute per receiver: DC offset of I and Q (counts), I/Q RMS ratio, and mirror-image factor alpha fitted as X(-k)=alpha*conj(X(k)) over bins 2-12 of the drift-removed coherent mean chirp. Each change restored to stock before the next; restores reproduced stock values.

findings.0x61: RX2 I DC offset, +1 step = +450 counts (0x20: -433). Linear both ways. Small side effect: RX2 image phase about +3 deg/step.
findings.0x63: RX2 I DC offset, opposite sense: +1 step = -461 counts.
findings.0x62: RX2 Q DC offset, +1 step = +514 counts.
findings.0x64: RX2 Q DC offset, opposite sense: +1 step = -456 counts.
findings.0x76: 0x21->0x22 removed the signal on BOTH receivers (outputs ~0, reflector gone). Restoring 0x21 recovered fully. Function unknown; handle with care.
findings.0x5B, 0x5C: +1 step: no measurable change in these metrics.
findings.0x5D: +1 in either byte: no measurable change in these metrics.

conclusions: 0x61-0x64 are differential DC-offset trims for RX2 only (I+/Q+/I-/Q- pattern), not I/Q gain or phase trims.
No RX1 offset trim found yet; none of the tested registers changes the mirror-image (I/Q mismatch) level usefully.
The mirror is a stable per-receiver property: RX1 about -13.8 dB, RX2 about -17.1 dB (bins 2-12).
